programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: As spring arrives in the Arctic, a mother polar bear emerges from her den with two tiny cubs. At the other end of the planet, winter arrives and emperor penguins are plunged into darkness for four months, enduring the coldest temperatures on the planet.

programme.title: The Girl Who Talked to Dolphins
programme.desc: Documentary telling the story of the most extraordinary experiment in the history of animal science. In the 1960s a powerful and charismatic scientist flooded a house. He then invited a young woman to live there full-time with a dolphin.

programme.title: Vienna: Empire, Dynasty and Dream
programme.desc: Simon Sebag Montefiore follows the Habsburgs to their dramatic demise. From his struggles with Napoleon III and Bismarck and the suicide of his son Rudolf, to the assassination of his beautiful wife Sisi, Emperor Franz Josef's empire and his family proved impossible to control.

programme.title: Rise of the Nazis
programme.desc: In the 1960s and 70s, the Second World War is a distant memory, but a few diehards are determined to hunt down thousands of Nazi war criminals. Many of whom are living in plain sight.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: A look at mountains, beginning with the birth of a mountain at one of the lowest places on Earth, and ending at the summit of Everest. Experience the full force of an avalanche in the Rockies, where grizzlies survive the harsh winters deep inside the dangerous slopes, and fly alongside demoiselle cranes as they attempt to cross the Himalayas.

programme.title: The Good Life
programme.desc: Wanting to sweep the chimney and catch fleas, Tom and Barbara face the dilemma of keeping the fleas from catching Margo and Jerry.

programme.title: Yes, Minister
programme.desc: A normally efficient local council is late with some paperwork, and Sir Humphrey wants to make an example of them.

programme.title: Billy Connolly: Big Banana Feet
programme.desc: Billy Connolly travels around Ireland in 1975 with a new set of comedy material.

programme.title: Face to Face
programme.desc: Jeremy Isaacs talks to Scottish comedian Billy Connolly about stand-up comedy, bodily functions and the night someone set fire to his hair.

programme.title: Billy Connolly: Made in Scotland
programme.desc: A look at the life and influences of Billy Connolly, featuring Eddie Izzard, Ross Noble, Micky Flanagan, Lord Grade, Tracey Ullman, AL Kennedy, Val McDermid, Sharleen Spiteri and Eddi Reader, showing a true reflection of his far influence.

programme.title: Billy Connolly: Made in Scotland
programme.desc: Billy goes back to the Scotland of his childhood where he reveals that knitted woolly swimming trunks were not a figment of his imagination. Featuring personal accounts and interviews from famous faces in Billy's life.

programme.title: The Trials of Oscar Pistorius
programme.desc: When a judge is assigned to the Oscar Pistorius trial, the world watches closely. In this case, a judge, and not a jury, decide the defendant's fate. The judge, Thokozile Masipa, is a highly respected scholar who grew up in the Soweto Township as a child of Apartheid. Despite the dignity with which she attempts to conduct the trial, no-one can stop it from becoming a televised tabloid circus.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: Taking an epic journey following the descent of the planet's mightiest rivers from their mountain sources to the sea. programme.title: What Are UFOs?

programme.title: Wildlife on One
programme.desc: A look at the life of ring-tailed lemurs on the African island of Madagascar who live in female-dominated gangs and continually fight for territory with their neighbours.

programme.title: Tribe
programme.desc: While living with the Babongo tribe of Gabon in West Africa, Bruce Parry undergoes an initiation ceremony which involves taking a powerful hallucinogen that lasts for three days.

programme.title: Eileen Atkins Remembers... Mrs Dalloway
programme.desc: In 1997, the film version of Virginia Woolf's Mrs Dalloway was released in cinemas, based on a screenplay by Dame Eileen Atkins and with her friend Vanessa Redgrave playing the title role, a party-throwing socialite remembering the freedoms of her younger life. Here, we join Eileen Atkins looking back just as her heroine does - telling the story of her lifelong fascination with Woolf and recalling how she took on the challenge of adapting of one of the 20th century's great novels for the big screen, and ended up winning the praise of the critics of the day, who called the resulting film 'sensitive', 'delicate' and 'compelling'.

programme.title: Mrs. Dalloway
programme.desc: As society hostess Clarissa Dalloway prepares for another of her legendary parties, she finds herself haunted by figures and scenes from her passionate youth.

programme.title: Wildlife on One
programme.desc: David Attenborough looks at how research has finally revealed the secret behind the remarkable sticking power of the gecko's foot. This discovery could offer truly futuristic ways of sticking objects together, and may even help NASA to explore distant planets. Including a look at the urban-dwelling tokay gecko that happily resides alongside the citizens of Bangkok as one of the few reptiles tolerated in homes.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: This edition is all about Earth's final frontier - caves. Deer Cave in Borneo is a daytime retreat for five million bats, and their droppings support an entire community of creatures. Troglodytes like the Texas cave salamander and Thailand's cave angel have neither eyes nor pigment, and the entire populations of both are found in just a couple of caves.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Celia Imrie explores the story behind Francis Ford Coppola's acclaimed Godfather series. Through interviews and insights from leading cast members Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, James Caan, Robert Duvall and Coppola himself, we discover how this tale of family betrayal, shocking violence, a horse's head and a bed resulted in two films that are widely considered amongst cinema's greatest achievements of the 1970s.

programme.title: The Godfather
programme.desc: The violent story of a Mafia family fighting to establish supremacy in the American business world following World War II, where an assassination attempt leaves Vito Corleone too ill to run the family business.

programme.title: The Godfather, Part II
programme.desc: Vito struggles to make a living, legally or illegally, for his wife and family in 1910s Little Italy, while Michael Corleone's 1950s business expansion and lust for power leads to paranoia and the destruction of his family.

programme.desc: Screenwriter and playwright Abi Morgan has worked across a diverse array of themes and genres for more than 25 years. programme.title: Chwedlau Tinga Tinga
